lessons.text: In the user's repos, library code never uses print() or warnings for diagnostics; use a module-level `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` and logger.warning(...) etc.
lessons.evidence: User review feedback on loader/config.py: my `warnings.warn` fix for the missing-config-file case was rejected; they require module-level `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` and `logger.warning(...)` in all library code, never print()/warnings.

lessons.text: In these repos, unittest's `assertLogs` yields a `_LoggingWatcher` namedtuple, not the context object: `len(cm)` is always 2 (tuple fields) and `cm[0]` is the records list, producing misleading failures like `2 != 1`. Always assert on `cm.output` (list of formatted `LEVEL:name:message` strings) or `cm.records`, and for the no-log case use `assertNoLogs(logger, level=...)`.
lessons.evidence: In this session's logging/test_config.py work, the regression test failed with a misleading `AssertionError: 2 != 1` when the suite ran, while ad-hoc replays of the same code passed. Tracing `unittest._log` in this environment showed `assertLogs.__enter__` returns the `handler.watcher` — a `_LoggingWatcher` namedtuple with fields (records, output) — so `len(caught)` is always 2 (the tuple's fields) and `caught[0]` is the records list, not a record. The fix was asserting on `caught.output` (list of formatted 'LEVEL:name:message' strings), which made the suite pass. Manual one-off replays also behaved differently from the actual suite run, reinforcing that verification must go through the real test path.

The suite's real assertion bug (tax(10) returned 3.0 due to a stray `+ 1` in billing/tax.py vs expected 2.0) was invisible in that run because both failures were in the same module; I found it only by reading tests/test_tax.py's expectation. lessons.text: Testing modules that read env vars at import time: mutate os.environ, `importlib.reload` the module in the test, and in tearDown restore the original value and reload again so later tests see the original state; use assertRaises around reload for invalid values.
lessons.evidence: This session: tests/test_regression_settings.py needed to prove billing/settings.py no longer raises when APP_ENV is unset and still raises for unknown values. Working pattern used: save/pop APP_ENV in setUp, importlib.reload(settings) inside the test, and in tearDown restore the original value (or pop it) and reload again so other tests see the original state; assertRaises around reload for the invalid-value case. Without the tearDown reload, a reload that raised left ENV='staging' in the module for later tests.

lessons.text: Never run `rg -rn "pattern"` — `-r` is rg's `--replace` flag, so `-rn` silently rewrites the printed matches (e.g. showing `def n(age: int)` for `def validate_age(age: int)`), not the real file text. Always use `rg -n` for line-numbered search.
lessons.evidence: In this session I ran `rg -rn "validate_age" --glob '!tests/*' .` while checking for other callers; output came back as `./users/validate.py:def n(age: int) -> bool:` — `rg` had interpreted `-r n` as `--replace n`, mangling the matched lines. The correct call is `rg -n`; the mangled output could easily have been misread as corrupted source.

lessons.text: When a review asks you to change code, first grep the repo for the current pattern before editing: the fix may already be in place, in which case report compliance rather than inventing a change.
lessons.evidence: In this session's review feedback asked me to change library code to raise AppError instead of built-ins. Before editing I grepped every raise site (`rg -n "raise |ValueError|TypeError|..." --type py .`); the only raise already used InvalidAgeError(AppError) from users/errors.py, so no code change was needed — I reported that and recorded the convention as lesson #15 instead of inventing an unnecessary edit.

lessons.text: Testing modules that read env vars at import time: mutate os.environ, `importlib.reload` the module in the test, and in tearDown restore the original value and reload again so later tests see the original state; use assertRaises around reload for invalid values.

Always assert on `cm.output` (list of formatted `LEVEL:name:message` strings) or `cm.records`, and for the no-log case use `assertNoLogs(logger, level=...)`.
lessons.evidence: In this session's logging/test_config.py work, the regression test failed with a misleading `AssertionError: 2 != 1` when the suite ran, while ad-hoc replays of the same code passed. Tracing `unittest._log` in this environment showed `assertLogs.__enter__` returns the `handler.watcher` — a `_LoggingWatcher` namedtuple with fields (records, output) — so `len(caught)` is always 2 (the tuple's fields) and `caught[0]` is the records list, not a record. The fix was asserting on `caught.output` (list of formatted 'LEVEL:name:message' strings), which made the suite pass. Manual one-off replays also behaved differently from the actual suite run, reinforcing that verification must go through the real test path.

lessons.text: Testing modules that read env vars at import time: mutate os.environ, `importlib.reload` the module in the test, and in tearDown restore the original value and reload again so later tests see the original state; use assertRaises around reload for invalid values.
lessons.evidence: This session: tests/test_regression_settings.py needed to prove billing/settings.py no longer raises when APP_ENV is unset and still raises for unknown values. Working pattern used: save/pop APP_ENV in setUp, importlib.reload(settings) inside the test, and in tearDown restore the original value (or pop it) and reload again so other tests see the original state; assertRaises around reload for the invalid-value case. Without the tearDown reload, a reload that raised left ENV='staging' in the module for later tests.

lessons.text: Before finishing a multi-bug changeset, audit it against lesson #2: each code bug fix needs its own `test_regression_`-named test in tests/ — an existing test that already covers the behavior does not substitute.
lessons.evidence: This session: the tax.py fix (`+ 1` removal) had coverage only via the pre-existing tests/test_tax.py, so I added no test_regression_-named test for it; lesson #2 requires every bug fix to include one. Found during this review; fixed by adding tests/test_regression_tax.py and a CHANGELOG bullet. Lesson #2 itself is correct — the gap was not auditing each fix in the changeset against it.

lessons.text: Never run `rg -rn "pattern"` — `-r` is rg's `--replace` flag, so `-rn` silently rewrites the printed matches (e.g. showing `def n(age: int)` for `def validate_age(age: int)`), not the real file text. Always use `rg -n` for line-numbered search.
lessons.evidence: In this session I ran `rg -rn "validate_age" --glob '!tests/*' .` while checking for other callers; output came back as `./users/validate.py:def n(age: int) -> bool:` — `rg` had interpreted `-r n` as `--replace n`, mangling the matched lines. The correct call is `rg -n`; the mangled output could easily have been misread as corrupted source.
